c0_01: 1219. // Khwarazm, / an Islamic empire in Central Asia, stretching from today's Uzbekistan to Iran.
c0_02: Its great cities sat behind towering walls, / the perfect defense against Mongol horsemen.
c0_03: And yet, every one of those walls came down, / and Khwarazm itself vanished with them.
c0_04: So how did the Mongols / bring down Khwarazm?
c0_05: The Mongol Empire, part two. / Let's begin.
c1_01: When word came that the Mongols were coming, / Khwarazm had two options.
c1_02: Meet them head-on in the open field, / or hold out behind the walls.
c1_04: It broke its great army into pieces, / and shut a piece inside every city.
c1_05: The logic went like this. / "Mongol cavalry is terrifying in the open, / but it can't climb a wall."
c1_06: "Just hold out behind the walls, / and the Mongols will tire and go home."
c1_07: On top of that, the Shah didn't trust his own generals. / Instead of handing the army to one commander, he scattered it across his cities, / and threw away his biggest weapon: sheer numbers.
c1_08: The Mongols did the exact opposite. / They split their army into four columns, / and struck everywhere at once.
c1_09: The first column surrounded the border city of Otrar.
c1_10: The second marched upriver, to the cities in the south. / The third followed the river north.
c1_11: And the fourth, / Genghis Khan's main army… // slipped into the desert, unseen by any city, / so the enemy had no idea where it was.
c1_12: Now Khwarazm's plan started falling apart.
c1_13: When one city came under attack, / the army in the next city was supposed to ride to its rescue. / But the moment they stepped outside the gates, / they were in open country.
c1_14: Exactly where Mongol cavalry fought best.
c1_15: So the cities couldn't help each other. / Each one had to fight alone.
c1_16: Overall, Khwarazm had far more men. / But in front of any single city, / the Mongols always had more.
c1_17: It didn't matter if a siege took months. / They left a small force to pin the city down, / and the rest moved on to the next one.
c1_18: Otrar held out for five months.
c1_19: But how do tens of thousands of horsemen / cross a desert with no water and no roads?
c2_01: Between the Syr Darya and the Amu Darya rivers / lay the Kyzylkum Desert.
c2_02: Khwarazm believed no large army could cross it, / so it left the desert side unguarded.
c2_03: But the Mongols / knew how to cross it.
c2_05: At the edge of the desert stood a small town. / When its people saw the Mongol horde, / they didn't dare to fight.
c2_06: A Mongol envoy promised their lives would be spared if they surrendered, / and the town opened its gates without a fight.
c2_07: From the people who surrendered, the Mongols picked a man who knew the desert paths, / and forced him to lead the way.
c2_08: What he knew was a route / linking hidden wells across the desert, / a route no Khwarazmian soldier was watching.
c2_09: He walked at the very front of the column, / pointing the way to the next well.
c2_11: Every Mongol soldier rode with several spare horses. / Crossing the desert, the horses far outnumbered the men.
c2_12: But desert wells are small. / They only give so much water a day.
c2_13: If everyone marched down one road, / the units in front would drink the wells dry, / and the ones behind would find nothing but empty wells.
c2_14: So the Mongols spread out into several columns, / each using its own wells.
c2_16: Mongol soldiers carried dried meat / and dried milk curds they could mix with water.
c2_17: No grain wagons meant / no wheels stuck in the sand.
c2_18: And it was late winter, / the coolest time of year in the desert.
c2_19: Bukhara's defenders were watching the river to the east.
c2_20: But the Mongols didn't come from the river. / They came out of the desert, behind the city.
c2_21: In a panic, the garrison tried to slip out of the city at night. / But outside the gates lay open country.
c2_22: With the garrison crushed, / the townspeople opened the gates themselves.
c2_23: But inside Bukhara stood a second fortress, / a citadel on a hill.
c2_24: The remaining soldiers retreated into it, / and held on to the end.
c2_25: So how did the Mongols / break that citadel?
c3_01: The Mongols had siege experts. / Engineers they'd brought back from their wars with the Jin.
c3_02: They didn't drag heavy catapults across the country. / They carried the parts on horseback, / and built the machines right in front of the walls.
c3_03: These catapults were powered by people pulling ropes.
c3_04: A stone sat at one end of a long beam. / Dozens of men yanked the ropes on the other end all at once, / and the beam whipped around and hurled the stone.
c3_05: When they ran out of stones, / they reportedly cut down trees, soaked the logs in water, and threw those instead.
c3_06: But in front of the walls was a deep moat. / To reach the walls, it had to be filled.
c3_07: So the Mongols brought in people from the cities they'd already taken, / and made them carry earth and wood to fill the moat.
c3_08: The defenders on the walls had no choice but to shoot. / At their own people.
c3_09: In the end, Bukhara's citadel fell.
c3_10: But the Mongols' strength / wasn't only on the battlefield. // They were masters of psychological warfare, too.
c4_01: Before they ever reached a city, / they sent a rumor ahead.
c4_02: The message they sent / was a threat. // "Open your gates, / and we will spare your lives. / But resist us, / and we will break your walls, take everything you own, / cut down every last one of you, armed or not, / and burn your city to the ground."
c4_03: And what happened to the cities that resisted / spread through the mouths of survivors they let go on purpose.
c4_04: The rumor traveled faster than the Mongols. / Before the army even arrived, / some cities opened their gates on their own.
c4_05: Breaking one city took months. / The rumor opened city after city in days. // And so the Mongols took Khwarazm with ease.
c5_01: And so the Mongols conquered Khwarazm, / the Islamic empire of Central Asia.
c5_02: To the west, all that remained / was the land of today's Russia, and Europe.
c5_03: And the first to ride down that road / were twenty thousand horsemen led by Jebe and Subutai.
c5_04: The Mongol Empire series / continues in part three.
